13B.7 All the labor of man is for his mouth.

precepts.text: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man. That tells you what the thing of Ecclesiastes 1:9 is.
precepts.point: There is no remembrance of former things. Why? Because the spirits from the past return to the future.
precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. What is the thing? Solomon tells you in chapter 6: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.” The thing is man on earth.

So “that which is done is that which shall be done”: whether man keeps the commandments or does not keep the commandments. “and there is no new thing under the sun.” From the time of Genesis, as it has been is going to be so in these last days. There are no new incidents on this earth; the things done by man are the things that were done in the past. And “There is no remembrance of former things”, because the spirits from the past return to the future.

Paul says the same in different words: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Written for our learning today, because the things done in the past reoccur. In a Christian mind everything is new; but nothing is new. To deal with these reoccurring events, we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors.

Ezra shows it too: “I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is a circle, “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” It is a continual event that reoccurs over and over. And the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets”, comparing one thing to another.

That is why what we read in Daniel 3, Nebuchadnezzar setting up his golden image, is coming to pass again with the Trump administration and the golden statue the pastors prayed over. The man that hath been is the man that shall be.

precepts.text: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man. So he explains it: the thing that have been is man.
precepts.point: The thing that hath been is that which shall be, and there is no new thing under the sun. Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? It hath been already of old time, which was before us: before our generation, it was in the past. And there is no remembrance of former things.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
What is the thing that hath been? Solomon names it: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man”. So he explains it himself: the thing that have been is man.

Just like the wind, the sun, the moon and the rivers have a flow, likewise man: we come and we go. You and I have been here before, in different cycles of life. That is why it is called deja vu, a French term that literally means already seen: the sensation of having already experienced a situation even though you know it is happening for the first time.

Already seen, because you are already meant to be there. The prophets saw things that came to pass. When the prophets saw us going on slave ships, we had to live out what they saw. So when John saw America in flames, we have to live out what John already saw. We are catching up to the prophecies, and what leads up to them is already set in motion. You can't change it.

precepts.text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men. Peter understood that common was tied to evil.
precepts.point: And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. The subject matter of the cleansing is man; and to explain that cleansing, Peter would have to use the Old Testament.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Peter answered the vision, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” To understand what he meant by common, go to Solomon: “There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men”.

Common is tied to evil. Peter understood that. So when he said he had never eaten anything common, he was not only talking about meat. In other words: I have never done sin, I have never dealt with sin, I have never dealt with people that were evil.

That is why the vision had to be explained to him. The sheet let down from heaven was not about food; it was about men, and Peter was being told to go among people he had counted as common.

precepts.text: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man. The thing that repeats is man himself.
precepts.point: Why this matters: what was done to us in slavery is a circle coming back around again. God's judgment is as a ring. Slavery is not over; the white man put on a smile, and now he is showing his real face. Like Antiochus, who died long ago, yet the scripture says he shall stand up against the Prince of princes: the same spirit comes back and does the same thing again.
precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. What is the thing that hath been? Solomon says: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man”. So the thing is man.

Read Ecclesiastes 1:9 again with that: “and that which is done is that which shall be done”. The same thing man did in the past, he is going to come back and do again. “there is no new thing under the sun.” If you were wicked in the past, you are going to be wicked again when you come back on the earth. That is why the scripture says he that is righteous, let him be righteous still, and he that is evil, let him be evil still. If you are righteous, you will gravitate to righteous brothers and sisters; if you are wicked, to wicked people.

Why is this important? Because what was done to us in slavery is a circle coming back around. God's judgment is as a ring. Slavery isn't over; the white man put a fake smile on his face, and now he is showing his real face. It is the same people coming back to do the same thing. Antiochus died long ago under the Greeks, yet the scripture says he shall stand up against the Prince of princes, because the same spirit that came against the holy people is going to do it again.

So just as Egypt said, the children of Israel “are more and mightier than we”, and “let us deal wisely with them”, America, spiritual Egypt, does the same today: the census, abortions and Planned Parenthood, changing laws as we become the majority. The thing that repeats is man himself.

precepts.text: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man. So the thing that is, is man. Going back to Ecclesiastes 1:9, what man does on the earth is what shall be done again.
precepts.point: Whether man keeps God's laws or does not keep God's laws, that which is done is that which shall be done.
precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. What is “The thing that hath been”? Solomon names it: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.” It is known that it is man. So the thing that is, is man.

Go back to Ecclesiastes 1:9 with that understanding. The thing that hath been is man, and it is that which shall be. “and that which is done is that which shall be done”: what man does on the earth, whether he keeps God's laws or doesn't keep God's laws, is what shall be done again. “and there is no new thing under the sun”: what happened in the past is what will happen again in these last days.

That is why the class goes back to Genesis. Cain would not bring the offering God required; sin lay at the door, and his desire was unto Satan, who ruled over him. His seed built the city Enoch: tents and cattle, buying and selling with unrighteous pricing; the harp and organ, and not holy music; Tubal-cain and every artificer in brass and iron, weapons; Lamech avenged seventy and sevenfold, wiping out a whole line. The sons of God took wives of all which they chose, the earth was filled with violence, and God destroyed it.

Think about the great cities today, like New York City: murder, wicked music, buying and selling, stealing, the wife looking over at the white woman or the Chinese woman. The same thing going on now is what was going on back then, because man is what he was.

points: There is an evil common among men: a man to whom the Most High has given riches, wealth, and honor so that he wants nothing his soul desires, yet is not given the power to eat of it, and a stranger eats it instead.
This is called vanity and an evil disease, for the wealth profits the man nothing when he has no power to enjoy the labor of his own hands.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 6: The Vanity of Wealth Without the Power to Enjoy It

points: Though a man beget a hundred children and live many years, if his soul is not filled with good and he has no burial, an untimely birth is better than he.
The untimely birth comes in with vanity and departs in darkness, having seen nothing, yet it has more rest than the man who lived and saw no good.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 6: The Vanity of Wealth Without the Power to Enjoy It

points: Though a man live a thousand years twice told and yet see no good, all go to one place, and length of days without the enjoyment of them is empty.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 6: The Vanity of Wealth Without the Power to Enjoy It

points: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is never filled, so the wise man in this has no advantage over the fool.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 6: The Vanity of Wealth Without the Power to Enjoy It

points: Better is the sight of the eyes, the good a man actually has before him, than the wandering of the desire that is never satisfied; this too is vanity and vexation of spirit.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 6: The Vanity of Wealth Without the Power to Enjoy It

points: That which has been is already named and known to be man, and man may not contend with the Most High, who is mightier than he.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 6: The Vanity of Wealth Without the Power to Enjoy It

points: The more a man multiplies words and things, the more he increases vanity, and no man knows what is truly good for him in the few days of his vain life, nor what shall be after him under the sun.
